findings: The complete finite singlet-pairing Hamiltonian, unrestricted equilibrium occupation space, local Sz operator, initially excited probe continuum and its normalized coupling spectrum uniquely specify sample-absorption rates. No lifetime broadening, parity restriction or self-consistent gap law is hidden.

The starter constructs the full Hermitian doubled-Nambu matrix and the correct thermal normal propagators. Its normal spectral convolution is the exact positive response of independent effective normal spin channels, but discards the pair covariance between physical spin channels. This is a physical factorization closure.

The oracle adds the anomalous contraction with the fermionic Wick minus sign. The Nambu covariance uses 1-f(E), so sums of its signed eigenenergies correspond to positive sample excitation frequencies. Physical electron indices avoid a doubled-space factor-of-two error.

The independent reference builds all64 fermionic occupation states with Jordan-Wigner signs, diagonalizes the many-body Hamiltonian, and sums pn times squared local-spin transition matrix elements at Em-En>0. The public coupling spectrum already contains2*pi and its Gaussian weight is intentionally unnormalized; the reference implements that convention.

Normal pairing0 calibration makes pair covariance vanish and identifies detector gain. Paired local-spin spectra retain nonzero signals, so the hidden comparison need not rely on a conserved global-spin zero or numerical cancellation.

This shares BCS background with superconducting-heat but tests a different physical approximation: independent spin covariance versus gap-edge energy weighting of an already included heat-coherence term. It is a distinct task, not an independent theoretical principle.
Public files supply apparatus/operator/preparation and API, without an anomalous-covariance correction, Wick formula or mandated representation.
